mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 8.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8.5% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakness in consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing contraction regime (INDPRO < 95.0), a decline in industrial production signals reduced corporate output and potential earnings cuts, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A positive quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates a strengthening economy, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 is positive, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals a potential for monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market boom (HOUST > 600.0 thousand units), strong housing activity boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 600.0, or the Rank IC for the regime condition is below 0.03.
